rv.q: First Folio has staged a beautiful and timeless production.

By the end, when Bias’s Jo draws up a trunk in the attic—the scene of so much joy despite economic deprivation in the early lives of the March sisters—and begins writing their story, it’s nearly impossible to keep tears from falling.
Director Melanie Keller moves the show along at a quick pace that keeps the viewer enthralled.
The problem, however, is that the current production often loses sight of the main point of the story and thus falls short in many ways.

cn.t: Critics largely praise this faithful adaptation of the beloved classic, with strong marks for Heather Chrisler's script that honors Alcott's timeless coming-of-age story, though one reviewer finds the production less impressive.
